verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents a tap-trust model in which tapping a third-party repository does not grant whole-tap trust and users install fully qualified items to trust only those items. That is a first-party supply-chain protection against untrusted packages, and a community comment welcomes the new tap trust feature. Nothing in the pack shows a minimum-release-age or cooldown control: one user explicitly asks for a cooldown after a new release reached Homebrew within about 85 minutes. There is also no evidence of blocking install or lifecycle scripts. Missing for 10: minimum release age/cooldown enforcement, blocking of install or lifecycle scripts, in-depth docs on how tap trust is enforced and configured, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can turn on protections against malicious packages, such as blocking lifecycle scripts or enforcing a minimum release age
